instruction:
Update the repo with model selection use on,y mit

Push it to main so I can test it on the live site
scope: Add an MIT-only model catalog and picker: Phi-1.5 (798633984 tensor bytes, smaller default), Phi-2 (1564948480 bytes), and existing Phi-4-mini instruct (2158049280 bytes). Show upstream memory estimates and base-model quality/iPad limitations.

Pin the new immutable model revisions, config/compiled-library integrity hashes, tensor minima and original Microsoft MIT notices. Preserve the existing patched WebLLM runtime, its Apache-2.0 notice and Phi-4 cache identity. Reject non-MIT catalog entries in the builder and browser loader.

Persist selected model ID; use that model record/minimum and identify it in diagnostics. Disable selection during initialization. After initialization, switching revokes the previous provider and reloads before another allocation. Failed initialization also requires reload; do not delete source data or model caches.

Add authored selection/license/error tests and a real Chromium picker workflow with explicit runtime/GPU fixtures, integrated into the existing CI/deployment browser runner. Update affected guides and result/documentation indexes. Publish to main at the user’s explicit request; verify the actual deployed site separately.
Preserve source-answer rules, provenance, imported sources, frozen evaluations and the zero-paid-provider constraint. Do not publish private uploaded device reports.
validation: Fetched the two added models’ immutable upstream MIT notices, MLC configurations, ndarray metadata and compiled libraries; retained hashes/byte counts in evaluation/model-selection/asset-verification.json. Total tensor sizes and maximum per-tensor sizes are computed from the pinned metadata. Model weights were not downloaded.
8 Python asset tests pass, including catalog/default/immutable-pin packaging checks and fail-closed non-MIT or modified-license rejection.

17 loader/state/DOM/runtime-API tests, 12 actual pinned GPU-negotiation-function checks, and 33 native-helper checks pass. GPU/runtime resource values and neural-success behavior are authored fixtures; no neural inference is claimed.

12 real Chromium/WebAssembly source-helper workflows plus 6 picker workflows pass. Picker checks cover MIT choices/sizes/default, explicit engine records, locked loading controls, report export, provider revocation/reload/persistence, retired selection recovery and non-MIT catalog rejection. No external model requests occurred.

UI script, browser transport, JavaScript API and crawler checks pass. Full regression, exact candidate archive, CI and postdeployment results are recorded by their corresponding runs; do not infer them from focused tests.

Full checkout Python regression passes: 877 tests. Documentation inventory, infrastructure linkage and generated handoff freshness checks also pass. These are checkout results, not exact-archive CI or postdeployment evidence.
limitations: Physical iPad loading and generation remain unverified. The supplied snapshots showed a later cached-weight failure with disposed-object/exit(1) after correct 512 MiB per-buffer negotiation; they do not prove total-memory exhaustion.

Phi-1.5 and Phi-2 are base models; instruction following and JSON planning may be unreliable. Smaller size and upstream working-memory estimates are not measured available RAM or guarantees for the selected context.

Browser success/switch tests replace GPU and engine execution with explicit authored fixtures. They do not establish model quality, complete live weight downloads or physical device compatibility. Existing source-answer limitations remain.

The selectable model licenses are MIT. Existing WebLLM remains Apache-2.0 with its original notices; this is not a relicensing of dependencies. No paid model service, training or hidden fallback is introduced.
next_steps: Complete the exact-head archive/CI gates, publish main as requested, and verify the model choices and existing source workflow against the newly deployed public URL. Record release/deployment identity in Actions rather than treating checkout tests as deployment evidence.

On iPad, reload the live page, choose Phi-1.5 and explicitly load it. Confirm successful initialization and a response; export the selected-model load report on failure. Do not treat percentage completion or the smaller default as a confirmed device repair.
For future changes, update this record from the latest instructions, preserve source/vendor/history bytes, review affected docs and regenerate/check the staged handoff.
